notes.text: - **Polygamy** = plural marriage, of two kinds: **polyandry** (Toda, Khasa) and **polygyny** – one husband, several wives (Bhil, Gond, Naga, Muria). Exam keys for "which tribe practises polygamy" answer **Toda**; strictly the polygynous tribes are polygamous too.

q: In which part of India would one find "Living Root Bridges"?
explanation: Living root bridges, made by training rubber-fig roots, are found in the Khasi and Jaintia hills of Meghalaya.

notes.text: - **Living root bridges** – **Meghalaya** (Khasi and Jaintia hills).

options: Irula of Tamil Nadu and Kerala
explanation: The Meena of Rajasthan are settled agriculturists, not hunters; Chenchu, Kamar and Irula are hunting and food-gathering tribes.

explanation: The Hornbill Festival (Kisama, 1-10 December) showcases the heritage of the Naga tribes of Nagaland.

q: The Maximum percentage of the tribal population in India consists of
explanation: Bhils are India's largest tribe (1.27 crore in 2001, 1.71 crore in 2011 – about 16% of all STs), ahead of Gonds, Santhals and Minas; Nagas are a group of smaller tribes.

notes.text: - Order: **Bhil (1,70,71,049) > Gond (1,32,56,928) > Santhal > Mina** (then Naikda, Oraon). Bhil ≈ 1.7 crore = about **16%** of STs (the "38%" in some books is the Bhil share of **MP's** STs, 37.7%).

explanation: The eight NE States hold about 1.24 crore of India's 10.43 crore STs – about 12%.

explanation: The Bhuria Committee (Dilip Singh Bhuria, 1994-95) examined tribal self-rule in Scheduled Areas and led to PESA 1996.

explanation: The 2013 PMO High-Level Committee on the socio-economic, health and educational status of tribes was chaired by Prof. Virginius Xaxa.

q: Which State in India having high percentage of rural population?
explanation: Himachal Pradesh is India's most rural State – about 90% rural (89.96% in 2011, 90.2% in 2001), just ahead of Bihar (88.7%).

notes.text: - Himachal Pradesh also led the rural share in 2001 (~90%), ahead of Bihar.
